objective: Optimize AdaSTEM execution while preserving scientific behavior and public compatibility.
primary_measure: Peak job memory across input preparation, partitioning, training, evaluation, and prediction together.
requirements: Preserve Pandas, DuckDB and Parquet inputs and existing model outputs.
Retain temporal-window prequerying, read-only database queries and parallel ensemble execution.
Preserve intended constant predictions in single-class stixels and missing coverage behavior.
Retain community-project custom gridding, stixel filtering and completely random rotations.
Correct bootstrap row multiplicity and test intentional behavior changes against a direct oracle.
Support arbitrary compatible base estimators without silently reducing model complexity or changing calibration.
Offer a simple Pandas-to-DuckDB API with automatic IDs, target alignment and temporary-file cleanup.
Bound queued work and offer explicit worker and inner-thread controls.
Measure end-to-end time and peak memory, plus phase times and memory peaks.
Keep optimization defaults portable across Apple Silicon and Linux HPC; label platform-specific measurements.
Treat GPU device memory and GPU timing separately from host memory and CPU execution; avoid automatic GPU concurrency assumptions.
Distinguish measured memory, logical data sizes, serialized models and estimates of estimator workspace.
Compare old and new implementations on identical fixtures, including real Acadian Flycatcher data.
Vary dataset size, feature count, ensemble count, input format and base estimator complexity.
Document local and single-node HPC use and the limitations of shared paths on multiple nodes.
Keep existing notebooks; add executed examples and update documentation after code and benchmarks.
Keep intermediate files temporary and avoid duplicating full source databases.
compatibility_exceptions: Bootstrap occurrences must be counted once rather than squared by duplicate-ID selection.
Logit aggregation must retain positive probabilities instead of incorrectly replacing them with zero.
Named Series targets must retain their values and validate index alignment.
validation_limits: Local measurements do not establish a memory bound for full HPC data or arbitrary estimators.
macOS physical footprint, Linux PSS/RSS, Slurm cgroup memory and GPU VRAM measure different quantities and must not be equated.
Multi-node execution requires shared accessible paths and is not validated on this machine.
Native DuckDB remains the default; shared numeric arrays are opt-in and require scratch space.
Small benchmark classifiers are execution tests, not evidence of improved probability calibration or copula accuracy.
